name: stack of three old worn tyres seen from above: top tyre as an elliptical grey rubber ring with rainwater in its hole, offset tread bands of the lower tyres below
label: wasteland_ruins/tyres

surfaces.part: top tyre ring with rainwater in the hole

answer.evidence: The width profile runs 7, 11, 13, then 16 across rows 4-8, then 14 at row 9. That is an ellipse of about 9 rows, from the back rim at row 1 to the front rim at row 9. The tyre ring is grey (L about 75-98) and the hole holds blue-grey water at rows 4-6. Row 9 is a darker front-edge line (x=4 reads #0e1720 there). Below it, rows 10-15 show offset dark and mid-tone tread bands (alternating #0e1720 and #3d4b51), which read as the front faces of the lower tyres. That gives about 6 front rows, so the drawing has a clear top ellipse and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small prop, about one tile in size. Its rubber ring, water hole and offset tread bands show roughly 5 distinct lightness steps. The measured facts support this: 12 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills of 5x5 or larger. Only 13% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark tone of the neighbouring material rather than a uniform black sticker line. The tread bands and water highlight give some grain, though less than the well or stall. It would sit acceptably next to the hedge and the other references without looking thinner or flatter.
